key: And Hilkiah the high priest said unto Shaphan the scribe: ‘I have found the book of the Law in the house of the LORD.’ And Hilkiah delivered the book to Shaphan, and he read it.
s: Sent by Josiah about the money for the Temple’s repair, Shaphan hears the high priest’s news; Rashi, on 22:8, reads the find as a scroll hidden under a course of stones when Ahaz burned the Torah, and Radak, on 22:8, as the scroll lying in its place beside the ark, the Torah forgotten in Manasseh’s long reign.

evidence.words: סֵפֶר הַתּוֹרָה מָצָאתִי. טְמֹן תַּחַת הַנִּדְבָּךְ, שֶׁהִטְמִינוּ שָׂם כְּשֶׁשָּׂרַף אָחָז אֶת הַתּוֹרָה. … ורחוק הוא זה … אלא מנשה מלך זמן רב שהרי מלך נ"ה שנה … והוא השכיח התורה מישראל … והיה חלקיהו מחפש בבית ה' ובבית קדש הקדשים ובדביר מצא ס"ת שהיה מונח במקומו מצד הארון
evidence.gloss: [Rashi:] I have found the book of the Law: hidden under the course of stones, where they had hidden it when Ahaz burned the Torah. [Radak, after reporting that account:] and this is far-fetched … rather, Manasseh reigned a long time, for he reigned fifty-five years … and it was he who made Israel forget the Torah … and Hilkiah, searching in the house of the LORD, in the Holy of Holies and the inner sanctuary, found a Torah scroll that was lying in its place beside the ark.
evidence.licence: Rashi Hebrew (Metsudah Tanach): CC-BY; Radak Hebrew (Radak on Nach): no licence stated by Sefaria, the text is centuries old. Own gloss; no copyrighted English quoted.

reason: verse.js ok, ref 2 Kings 22:8 at [330,8] match. Rashi on 22:8: the scroll was hidden under the course of stones when Ahaz burned the Torah. Radak on 22:8 reports that midrash, calls it far-fetched, and instead has the Torah forgotten under Manasseh’s fifty-five-year reign, with Hilkiah finding the scroll lying in its place beside the ark. The two genuinely differ; the sentence names both without resolving. Plain sense matches 22:3 to 22:7 (Shaphan sent about the money for repairing the house). Two editions named in src. entry-check ok, no warns.
